title: Chaos and the shoebox of photographs
learning_goal: See reversals in a three-mode model, understand why 'when' is unpredictable, and why the stationary distribution (a shuffled box of snapshots) is the stable object; meet crowd laws.
takeaway: The date of the next flip is unknowable, but the cloud of states is stable, and some laws hold only for the cloud.
notes: All scenes are ready (D4): numbers come from E1 (data/e1_finegrid.json, data/e1_samples_0.93.json, the digest) and from the prep module P4; no new data file is needed. The live RK4 integrations of 04.2, 04.4, 04.5 and 04.6 are illustrations, as in the site widget assets/interactif/gissinger.js; nothing they draw is quoted as a result. The T4 chapter card sits in the 3.2-s lead-in of 04.1, with staircase tier 0 lit (critique E1). Predict beats: an unnumbered one in 04.2 ('like clockwork?', hold 2.5 s) and Q4 in 04.4 (hold 3.0 s); on screen both read PREDICT only. Changes against the outline, to review: (1) 04.2 gains the 'clockwork' predict beat, which targets the misconception 'deterministic means regular' and sets up 04.4. (2) 04.3 says 'not every tick is a flip: an excursion can cross and come straight back' instead of 'most ticks are flips' (the site never quantifies the share, R:528). (3) 04.3 reads data/e1_finegrid.json, not the prototype proto/data/e1_rate.json (CONTRACT 5). (4) 04.4 answers 'only a short way ahead', not a flat 'no': six decimals give a horizon of about 150 time units (P4:814-818 with the exponent 0.089) against a mean wait of about 226 between crossings, and each extra decimal buys only about 25 units; this is the site's own argument (P4:1627) without overclaiming, since about half of the waits are shorter than the horizon. (5) 04.6 uses the snapshots at Gamma = 0.93 (outline: 0.9) so that 04.5, 04.6 and 04.7 share one setting and 04.7 drops the photos of the 04.6 shoebox; 05.2 can reopen the box at 0.93 (e1_samples_0.93.json has Ddot) or show a chip 'Γ = 0.9'. (6) The crisis chip of 04.2 avoids the symbol mu (D3): 'shown by Gissinger 2012 for another coefficient; expected, not proved, in Gamma'. Symbol sheet: the Lyapunov exponent is written in words (lambda is reserved for a knob) and physical time is never written as a bare t on screen (t is the generator's transport time from 06.2; the derivative dE/dt of 04.7 stays, as dB/dt does in ch01 and ch03); r_0 for the crossing rate, eps for dissipation. Badges: CONTEXT (04.1 published model, 04.5 ergodic theorem), MEASURED (04.2-04.4, 04.6), PROVED (04.7, Proposition 5), none on the question card. Lexicon: Gissinger and Lyapunov are pinned; 'Gamma' is spoken as a plain word, no new pin needed. Words budgeted at 125-130 effective words per minute against target_s; estimates use the assembler formula (146 raw words per minute, 0.9 s per paragraph break, holds, lead-in and tail). Adversarial review 2026-11-08: changelog and evidence in script/_review/ch04.md.

scenes.title: Three dials

params.read: ctx.data.e1.config.mu and .nu give the two coefficients shown in the equations (0.119, 0.1); nothing typed

sentences.text: Here is the caricature: three dials, linked by springs.
One is the {b}dipole{/}, the north-south part of the field.
One is the {b}quadrupole{/}, a four-pole part.
The third is a {u}flow{/} pattern, driven by a knob, {param}Gamma{/}.
Three short equations, from Gissinger, tie them together.
Flip both field dials, and the equations read the same.
Three dials, three numbers: the bottom step of the staircase.

scenes.title: Two whirlpools and a corridor

params.note: knob schedule and speeds are scene choices inside the known range of Gamma (0.80-1.00); the threshold window and the coefficients come from ctx.data.e1

sentences.text: Use two dials as a map: {b}quadrupole{/} across, {b}dipole{/} up.
With the knob low, the state circles in one whirlpool, and stays.
A mirror twin circles the mirror whirlpool: dipole down.
Each start is trapped. The dipole never changes sign.
Now turn {param}Gamma{/} up.
Just above zero point eight six, the whirlpools touch: a narrow corridor opens.
The state lingers on one side, then slips through. The {b}dipole{/} flips.
Nothing here is random. So, will the flips come like clockwork?
No. Long waits and short ones, irregularly.
The dipole's sign prints uneven stripes, like the seafloor.

labels: Will the flips come like clockwork?

formulas.tex: \text{E1 fine grid: no crossing for } \Gam \le 0.86;\ \text{crossings from } \Gam = 0.865
\text{Gissinger 2012, at } \Gam = 0.9\text{: crisis when the } Q \text{ coefficient passes } 0.11928

Corner needle M1 (Kit.needle corner: true) from 'map', flipping 180 degrees at every sign change of D. Trail: the last params.trail_units units, fading, segments with D > 0 in --b and D < 0 in --b-neg (polarity is a shade, never a new hue). On 'map-0.15': the D and Q dials of 04.1 slide in from the top and turn into the two axes (T1 morph, 1.2 s); the state dot appears and starts circling. On 'low': knob at 0.80; the trail fills the upper whirlpool; label 'one whirlpool'. On 'twin-0.15': a second dot starts at the exact mirror state (-Q, -D, V), drawn in --b-neg, and paints the mirror whirlpool below; label 'mirror whirlpool'. On 'trapped': the pen (M9) draws a closed loop around each whirlpool; the strip shows D never crossing zero; the mirror dot fades out at 'turn-0.5'. On 'turn': the knob turns from 0.80 to 0.86 in 3 s (detents), the whirlpool swells and stays on its side. On 'touch-0.15': the knob enters the green window and goes on to 0.87; the outlines of the two whirlpools touch at the centre; label 'corridor' with a pen arrow through the gap; reference lower-third 'Reference' / 'Gissinger 2012 · crisis shown for another coefficient' at 'touch+0.6' for 4 s, and the plain chip 'crisis in Γ: expected, not proved' beside the knob from 'touch+0.6' (critique C3; no mu or nu symbol anywhere). In setup, pick the starting state among params.candidates seeded states (Scene.rng('ic')) so that, with this knob schedule, D does not cross zero before 'flip' and first crosses within params.first_flip_window_s after 'flip' (deterministic search on ctx.at times); the dot slips through the corridor, the needle flips. On 'predict': PREDICT card top-centre 'Will the flips come like clockwork?' with two grey outline buttons 'A · regular' and 'B · irregular' (unnumbered predict beat; the 2.5 s hold comes from the script; the dot keeps circling, nothing new appears). On 'irregular': button B lights, the card slides out; the knob ramps to 1.00 in 3 s and the speed rises to params.units_per_s_fast, so several flips arrive at visibly uneven intervals; the polarity strip fills. On 'barcode-0.15': the polarity strip brightens and a small grey thumbnail of the 00.3 seafloor strip (40 % opacity) slides beside it, label 'seafloor · chapter 00' (visual callback only, no claim that the model is the Earth). Sound: page events window.__EVENTS__ = one 'needle' (two-note M1) per sign change of D, gain -18 dB, at most one per params.needle_min_gap_s; detents from the sfx list. Chip 'illustration · live integration of the model' (plain) under the phase map. Badge MEASURED top-right (the threshold comes from E1). Key colours: vermillion, green. Dense scene: encode crf 23.

scenes.title: Listen to the rate

sentences.text: Now count: one tick each time the {b}dipole{/} crosses zero.
Not every tick is a flip: an excursion can cross and come straight back.
Ticks per unit of time: the {metric}crossing rate{/}.
Up to zero point eight six: silence.
Just above, about two ticks per thousand time units.
At {param}Gamma{/} equal to one, about eleven.

labels: crossing rate = ticks per unit of time

scenes.title: Predict: when is the next flip?

params.lyapunov_source: en/prep/p4-systemes-dynamiques/index.qmd:1776-1778 (exercise 14, Gamma = 0.9: largest exponent +0.089 at T = 4000; Gissinger 2012: about 0.1)
params.horizon_rule: horizon = ln(attractor_size / delta0) / lyapunov_exponent = 155 model units; time runs from 'together' so that this horizon is reached at 'lost+0.3'
params.mean_wait_rule: 1 / y at Gamma = 0.9 of the series 'simulation (counted crossings)' of ctx.data.e1 (0.00442 -> 226), shown rounded to two significant figures

sentences.text: Set {param}Gamma{/} at zero point nine, and launch two copies, one millionth apart.
We know the state to six decimals. Can we predict the date of the next flip?
At first, the copies move as one.
But their gap nearly triples every eleven time units.
After about a hundred and fifty, they disagree completely.
The average wait between crossings is longer: over two hundred.
Each extra decimal buys only about twenty-five more time units.
So the forecast fades before the average wait ends. Only the statistics survive.

labels: We know the state to six decimals. Can we predict the date of the next flip?
A · yes: the equations are exact
B · only a short way ahead

scenes.visual: Render class dense2d. Predict beat Q4 of the outline; on screen it reads PREDICT only (no number, to avoid a clash with the question cards). Gamma = params.gamma (green chip 'Γ = 0.9'). Integrator as 04.2 (RK4, params.dt, coefficients from ctx.data.e1.config); copy A starts on the attractor after params.transient_units; copy B = copy A + params.delta0 on D. Typical pair, not an extreme one: in setup, among params.candidates seeded starting states (Scene.rng('pair')), keep the one whose gap first exceeds 0.5 closest to the horizon of params.horizon_rule; plain chip 'one example pair'. Layout: top panel (box x 160-1760, y 110-330): D(t) of copy A (solid --b) and copy B (solid --fg-2, 2 px, 70 %), drawn left to right as time runs, axis 'time (model units)' 0 to params.t_max_units; middle panel (Kit.plot, box x 160-1760, y 370-600, y log from 10⁻⁶ to 10, label 'gap between the copies', same time axis): the gap |A - B| in --fg, plus a dashed grey reference line of slope params.lyapunov_exponent from 10⁻⁶ at time 0; bottom: a ruler (y 640-720) from 0 to params.t_max_units. Corner needle M1 follows copy A. On 'twins-0.15': two dots launch from the same place; labels 'copy A' and 'copy B · 10⁻⁶ away'; time does not run yet. On 'predict': PREDICT card top-centre with the question of onscreen.labels and two grey outline buttons 'A · yes: the equations are exact' / 'B · only a short way ahead'; during the 3.0 s hold nothing new appears (the dots breathe). On 'together': time runs (rate set by params.horizon_rule): the two D traces overlap exactly; the gap creeps up along the dashed line. On 'apart-0.15': brace on the dashed line, '×e every 11 time units' (11 = 1/params.lyapunov_exponent, rounded). On 'lost-0.15': the D traces visibly part (one copy flips, the other does not) and the gap saturates near 1; a vertical marker at the horizon, 'six decimals used up · ≈ 150'. On 'wait-0.15': the ruler lights three marks: 11 'Lyapunov time ≈ 11', the horizon 'six decimals used up · ≈ 150', and the mean wait between crossings from params.mean_wait_rule, 'average wait between crossings ≈ 230', with a grey bracket showing the wait reaching past the horizon; source lower-third (kind 'source', data ctx.data.e1) at 'wait+0.4' for 4 s. On 'decimal-0.15': the horizon mark steps right twice by ln(10)/params.lyapunov_exponent (about 26 units each, so eight decimals reach about 205, still short of the average wait of about 226), each step labelled '+1 decimal ≈ +25'; never a third step, which would pass the wait mark (nine decimals: about 230) and contradict the narration. On 'answer': button B lights; the D traces and the gap curve dim to 35 %; a faint amber histogram silhouette fades in at the right as the bridge to 04.5. Badge MEASURED (mean wait from E1; the exponent was measured by the prep module's own code, P4 exercise 14). Key colours: vermillion, green (chip), amber only at the end. Never write the Lyapunov exponent with the letter lambda (the symbol sheet keeps lambda for a knob) and never write physical time as t on screen (t is the generator's transport time from 06.2): 'time' in words.

scenes.title: The long exposure

sentences.text: The path is lost, so leave the shutter open.
Each pass leaves a little light: a glow builds.
A copy started on the other side first paints the mirror image.
Given time, both paint the same glow.
Where does the {b}dipole{/} spend its time? Two humps, the same for both.
This reproducible glow is the stationary distribution.
Below the threshold, each start paints its own whirlpool.

labels: below the threshold: one whirlpool per start

formulas.tex: \text{time average along one long run} = \text{average over the glow}

chips: illustration · live integration of the model

scenes.visual: Render class dense2d. Gamma = params.gamma, shown as the green chip 'Γ = 0.93' from 'shutter' to the end (critique B6: the statement holds above the threshold only). Two panels side by side (x 140-900 and x 1020-1780, y 110-540), each a (Q, D) phase map with a long-exposure accumulation canvas: every integration step adds light where the state is (additive, log-scaled brightness; D > 0 half in --b, D < 0 half in --b-neg); under each panel an amber histogram of D (M5 first appearance, Kit.histogram, box y 570-700, range params.range_D, params.bins bins) built from the same visits. Integrator as 04.2 at params.units_per_s model units per second (a few dozen crossings during the scene). Copy A starts on the D > 0 side, copy B on the D < 0 side at a different, NON-mirror state (Scene.rng('b')), both after params.transient_units. On 'shutter-0.15': left panel only: the dot moves with a short trail, then a grey shutter icon opens and the trail stops fading; label 'long exposure'. On 'glow': light accumulates in the upper lobe; the left histogram grows one hump. On 'second-0.15': right panel and copy B: at first its glow is the mirror image of A's (lower lobe) and its histogram the mirror hump; labels 'copy A', 'copy B'. scenes.title: The shoebox

sentences.text: Now film the trajectory, one frame every two time units.
Neighbouring frames look alike.
Cut the film into frames.
Drop them in a shoebox, shake, and throw away the timestamps.
Pour the box out: the frames redraw the same glow.
Each frame is a snapshot: three dial readings, nothing more.
It carries no timestamp and no time order.
Yet the shoebox, plus the equations, answers many questions.
Averages, energy budgets, even how often the dipole crosses zero.

labels: a snapshot carries no timestamp and no time order
how often D crosses zero · with the equations · chapter 05

Gamma = 0.93 everywhere in 04.5-04.7 (one setting for the glow, the shoebox and the crowd law). Shoebox design (M-shoebox, first appearance): an open grey box (--matter outline, --matter-dark inside) of params.box size; it must be reusable as is by 06.4 (generated violet photos drop into it) and 05.2. On 'film-0.15': a horizontal film strip (grey frame with sprocket holes) slides in at y 140-300; each frame (160 x 120 px) shows the three small dials of 04.1 (D vermillion, Q light vermillion, V blue) at one instant of a live trajectory at Gamma = 0.93, one frame every params.frame_every_units model units (the E1 snapshot spacing), with a mono timestamp under it ('time 0', 'time 2', 'time 4' ...; never the letter t, which the symbol sheet keeps for the generator's transport time); the strip scrolls left; neighbouring frames differ only a little. On 'pour-0.15': the box tips; the frames pour out as points into a (Q, D) map (box x 560-1360, y 110-700) and multiply into the 8,000 reference snapshots of the data (2 px, params.point_alpha, --b where D > 0 and --b-neg where D < 0), which redraw the glow of 04.5; its outline sits under them as a grey dashed contour for comparison; label '8,000 snapshots · Γ = 0.93' (n from the data); white chip SIMULATED; source lower-third (kind 'source', data ctx.data.shoebox) at 'pour+0.6' for 4 s. On 'tags': three tags light up on their words: 'averages', 'energy budgets', and, dashed amber as a promise, 'how often D crosses zero · with the equations · chapter 05'. scenes.title: Crowd laws

sentences.text: Pick one photo. Its three dial readings give its energy.
From that photo alone, the equations tell how fast its energy changes.
Drop one marble per photo at that value.
Some photos are gaining energy, others losing it. The pile spreads wide.
Yet its average sits at zero.
Energy in equals energy out, on average.
Like a bank account: over the years, income matches spending, yet each day gains or loses.
This is a {metric}law of the crowd{/}. It holds for the shoebox, not for each photo.

labels: dE/dt, from the photo and the equations
rate of change of energy, dE/dt
true on average, not for each
one photo: no reason to be at 0

scenes.visual: Render class flat (Canvas histogram). The shoebox of 04.6 sits small at top-left. Amber histogram (M5, Kit.histogram, box x 360-1560, y 300-640, range params.range, params.bins bins; the half per cent of values beyond the range on each side is collected into small edge markers, never dropped); x axis 'rate of change of energy, dE/dt' with 0 marked; no count numbers. On 'energy-0.15': one photo slides out of the box and enlarges at the left: its three dials and readings; under it a grey bar 'energy E = ½ (Q² + D² + V²)'. On 'rate-0.15': an arrow on the energy bar points up or down with a length set by that photo's dEdt; label 'dE/dt, from the photo and the equations'. On 'marble-0.15': that value becomes an amber marble (8 px) that drops into its bin; then params.one_by_one more photos do the same one by one (params.one_by_one_s each, soft 'tick' page events at params.tick_gain_db), then the rest rain down in params.rain_s (bins accumulate, no physics, no bounce). On 'spread': the histogram breathes (plus or minus 1 % height, idle); labels 'losing energy' (left) and 'gaining energy' (right). On 'mean-0.15': an amber vertical marker drops at the sample mean, computed in setup from the dEdt array (it sits on 0 to the eye: mean 0.0002 against a spread of 0.43); label 'mean ≈ 0'; the pen (M9) circles it. On 'budget': the amber main-layer formula E[dE/dt] = 0 (onscreen.labels) above the histogram and the dashed-outline tag 'true on average, not for each' (the 'on average' tag style of 01.4). On 'bank-0.15': a small ledger card flashes in the top-right for 3 s (grey dashed chip 'SCHEMATIC · ledger', no numbers): daily bars up and down in --fg-2 and a running balance line that wanders and comes back to its starting level; label 'income = spending, on average' (preview of 07.5). question.en: How many *independent snapshots* does each setting need, and *how far apart* must they be saved?
question.say: How many independent snapshots does each setting need, and how far apart must they be saved?
question.fr: Combien d'instantanés indépendants faut-il pour chaque réglage, et à quel intervalle faut-il les enregistrer ?
question.why: Only long-run statistics are reproducible, and nearby frames are correlated: the plan wants 5,000 snapshots per 3D point; Taylor–Green now keeps 40 per point.
question.unblocks: Runs per point (n_traj 1 or 4), kept duration and snapshot spacing of the Taylor–Green campaign: data volume and GPU hours.
question.why_fr: Seules les statistiques de long terme sont reproductibles, et des images proches sont corrélées : le plan vise 5 000 instantanés par point 3D ; Taylor–Green n'en garde que 40 par point.
question.unblocks_fr: Nombre de trajectoires par point (n_traj 1 ou 4), durée gardée et intervalle entre instantanés de la campagne Taylor–Green : volume de données et heures GPU.
